memos.risk:
Risk officer read: the class is OPERATOR, which has been roughly break-even, but this brief has red flags that push it toward refusal. The curve is 100% bundle-controlled with top-5 buyers at 99.7% and sell-to-buy of 0.0009 in the first two minutes, so the operator bought at graduation and nobody else could sell. Pool depth is 931 SOL, so $20 is negligible in impact, but a 2.87x completer share and a 30-minute return of only +7% mean we'd be buying a coin whose insiders still hold almost everything.

Sane parameters if the desk insists on buying: $5 ticket, 20% stop, 15-minute hold. Refuse any size if the operator's sell pressure rises on the next check, if the top holders still hold most supply, or if drawdown from the high hits the stop before entry lands.

My recommendation: skip. Concentrated bundle control with near-zero sell depth is the setup where a dump is most likely to come with no exit liquidity.
memos.scout:
Best honest case FOR buying: limited. The brief shows 272 buyers and 18.9 SOL bought in the last 15 minutes, net flow +6.8 SOL, price up 1.4% over that window, and a 7.3% gain over 30 minutes with no drawdown from the high. Pool depth of 931 SOL means a $20 ticket would have modest impact. Those are the only signs of live demand.

But the demand looks operator-driven. Operator-class launch: 825 SOL bought from 30 wallets in the first two minutes, top-5 buyers hold 99.7% of early flow, a launch bot was present, and the bundle share is 100%. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was 0.0009. Recent demand is thin relative to the market cap of $5.8M, and sellers (33) are already starting to exit.

My read: this is not a case I can make honestly for buying now. The recent positive flow is real but sits on top of an operator-controlled supply structure, and that class has been break-even at best. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution after a thin rally. The curve is 100% bundled: one bundle holds the entire curve supply (bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0), and the first 2 minutes after graduation saw 825 SOL from 30 buyers, with the top 5 buyers taking 99.7% of buy flow. That is an operator-backed launch, and the operator is positioned to sell into any demand. Recent flow is already leaning toward exit: last 15 minutes show 12.12 SOL sold versus 18.91 bought, with 33 sellers. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a $20 ticket also means only a move above that band is profitable, and the 30-minute return of +7.3% and 1.4% last-15 return sit close to that threshold. Skip.
